conclusion: Below ~10% in blood: usually no attributable phenotype. Blood systematically under-represents the burden in post-mitotic tissue, so a low blood fraction does not exclude disease — measure urine or muscle before reassuring.
Roughly 10-30% in blood: maternally inherited diabetes and deafness is the usual presentation at this level.
Above ~30% in blood: MELAS-spectrum features become increasingly likely. Level correlates with severity but does not determine it.
No heteroplasmy fraction was measured in blood. Withhold: an absent measurement is not a low one, and the reference bin is not the default.
Below ~40% in muscle. The muscle threshold sits far higher than the blood one, which is why the same fraction means different things in the two tissues.
Above ~40% in muscle: MELAS-spectrum disease. Muscle reflects the burden in affected tissue far better than blood.
No heteroplasmy fraction was measured in muscle.
Below ~15% in blood for m.3271T>C. A different variant in the same gene, with its own threshold — which is why these bins carry a variant identity.
Above ~15% in blood for m.3271T>C: MELAS-spectrum features reported.
No heteroplasmy fraction was measured in blood for m.3271T>C.
